title: GRGM1200A PDS label and coefficient prefix
finding: 4pi fully normalized; reference radius 1738 km; DE430 principal axes. Archived model 1200/1200; this study uses 40,80,120 only.
limits: Header GM differs from label by 1.5 ppb. Model uses label GM 4902.80011526323 km3/s2. DE421 orientation approximation tested; no clone covariance or tide propagation.

title: GSFC GRGM1200A products
finding: GRAIL resolves global gravity; gravity and topography need matching PA frames. Coefficients, uncertainties and covariance-derived clones archived.
limits: Use establishes provenance, not independent validation of this propagator.

title: NAIF lunar frame kernel moon_080317.tf
location: Frames Specified; Comparison of PA and ME; Using this Kernel
finding: MOON_PA_DE421 uses binary PCK. PA and ME differ by ~0.02885 deg / 875 m; do not interchange them.
limits: DE421 PA is used as an explicitly approximate realization for DE430 gravity. A 0.01 deg offset sensitivity is not proof of exact frame equivalence.

title: NAIF SPK system and generic ephemeris kernels
location: SPK Required Reading: Computing States; cache manifest
finding: Actual de440s.bsp, naif0012.tls and lunar binary PCK were downloaded and used through SpiceyPy. Sun/Earth geometric vectors use NONE aberration correction.
limits: No GMAT, Orekit, STK or operational navigation solution was run.

title: Mesarch: Long-Term Orbit Operations for LRO, AAS-23-234
finding: 50±15 km science orbit: ~11 m/s per four weeks (~143 m/s/year). Frozen-orbit transition reduced maintenance to <5 m/s/year. Inclination drift ~0.4 deg/year; control would cost ~14 m/s/year. Momentum dumps typically 2-4 weeks; one-shot operations 7-40 min.
limits: Values belong to LRO's geometry and operational envelope. Its mass, arrays and flight hardware differ from the matched fixture; do not transfer its unloading cadence as a prediction.

title: Beckman and Lamb: Stationkeeping for LRO
finding: Specific 50/100 km circular-polar examples reach a 12 km mountain envelope in ~41/~150 days. Quasi-frozen 26x216 km, periapsis near 270 deg. Monthly apsis-rotation strategy; 150 m/s/year design allocation.
limits: Older LP gravity and particular initial geometry. A 12 km envelope is not a local terrain impact. Neither 41 nor 150 days is universal.

title: Emmert et al.: NRLMSIS 2.0
finding: Neutral densities depend on altitude, position, time, F10.7 and geomagnetic activity. This study actually runs MSIS 2.0 via pymsis 0.13.0.
limits: Fixed quiet/moderate/active proxy states are climatological sensitivity cases; not a storm forecast or solar-cycle history. Orbit-average profile held fixed during decay.

title: NASA/JPL Three-Body Periodic Orbits API
location: Data Output; system units; retrieved northern Earth-Moon L2 halo, long-period branch
finding: CRTBP rotating barycentric state, mass ratio and normalization retrieved. Chosen Jacobi 3.0901151159191, period 14.4554 days; catalogue stability index 170.405.
limits: Ideal circular Earth-Moon model. This is a reproducible nearby family example, not LUMIO's dated ephemeris trajectory. No unique calendar epoch exists for this autonomous model.

title: Topputo et al.: LUMIO current status and lessons learnt
location: p.7 §4.1 Fig.4; p.8 §4.3 and Table 4-1; p.10 Table 6-1
finding: Cj=3.09 quasi-halo. Annual stationkeeping mean 8.256 m/s, 3-sigma 15.79 m/s, 2-day cut-off. Budget disposal 0.97 m/s. Separate RCS total impulse 110 N s; 5 arcsec/66.7 ms relative pointing is a requirement.
limits: Web PDF text/page reviewed; direct local download denied 403. Published prediction, not flight evidence. Exact error covariances not restated in §4.3; do not silently import 2022 covariances.

title: Franzese et al.: Current status of LUMIO
finding: Earlier annual mean/3-sigma costs 1.86/4.34 m/s for 1 km,1 cm/s,2% error assumptions and 2-day cut-off.
limits: Historical optimistic result, superseded for planning by later 2024 figures. Search extraction accessible; local download denied. Not used as a budget baseline.

title: Cipriano et al.: Orbit Design for LUMIO
finding: Target-points control is coupled to navigation/execution uncertainty and timing. Cj=3.09 annual 3-sigma cost 28.1 m/s; disposal 3 m/s historical estimate.
limits: Earlier trajectory/control assumptions. 28.1 m/s supports a sensitivity allowance, not a current LUMIO requirement.

title: Giordano et al.: Design and Analysis of LUMIO Transfer Trajectory
finding: Operational quasi-halo is still generated from Cj=3.09. Phase B transfer uses WSB architecture; orbit choice rests on coverage, eclipse and maneuver trade.
limits: Transfer-focused paper does not validate this study's controller or establish a new operational annual maintenance budget.

title: ESA: LUMIO Phase C officially launched
finding: Phase C begun; potential launch 2028. Agency describes roughly 40000-80000 km distant farside observer.
limits: Schedule uncertain; source's continuous-visibility language is not a dark-surface exposure or whole-Moon coverage proof.

title: NASA Moon Fact Sheet
finding: Solar irradiance 1361 W/m2; Bond/geometric albedo 0.11/0.12; illustrative equatorial 95-390 K; surface ambient exosphere upper estimates ~2e5 particles/cm3.
limits: This study deliberately uses 0.12 as a rounded conservative reflectance fixture, not a measured Bond albedo. Exosphere drag bound uses all-argon mass and surface density at orbital altitude; not a local density prediction.

title: Purucker and Nicholas: Lunar internal magnetic field models
finding: Degree-170 crustal models from 30 km Lunar Prospector data; weak low-degree power; no present dynamo field.
limits: No crustal field model was propagated here. Lunar field scenarios 5/30/100 nT are declared engineering sensitivities, not validated percentile bounds.

title: NOAA NCEI World Magnetic Model
location: Mineral Exploration; WMM2025 technical report links
finding: Main surface field typically 20000-60000 nT. Dipole scaling supports tens of microtesla LEO comparison.
limits: LEO 50 microtesla is a conservative fixture, not a computed WMM orbit history.

title: CubeSpace CubeWheel product description CS-DEV.PD.CW-01
finding: CW0500: 50 mN m s at 6000 rpm,10 mN m,322 g,0.8 W at 2000 rpm,15 W nominal-torque peak. CW0162:16.2 mN m s,7 mN m,144 g.
limits: Web PDF reviewed; local fetch denied403. Wheel class examples only. Qualification and exported disturbance spectra require a mission-specific review; storage is not full usable array momentum.

title: Shields et al.: Characterization of CubeSat Reaction Wheel Assemblies
kind: measured component disturbance tests + simulated mission response
finding: BCT15 measured static0.38 g mm, dynamic27.59 g mm2; BCT1000.69/33.12; SI300.65/43.16. Tests in 50rpm steps, spectra to500Hz; resonances and harmonics matter.
limits: Historical purchased units, pre-vibration, not the CW0500. Rigid-body scaling from these imbalances does not establish integrated optical jitter.

title: Pong: ASTERIA on-orbit attitude and pointing performance
finding: Two-stage bus wheel plus focal-plane piezo control achieved0.5arcsec RMS over20minutes; wheel zero crossings and residual dipole affected operation.
limits: Different hardware, target and measurement interval; no transfer of0.5arcsec result to this lunar sensor.

title: GomSpace NanoProp CGP3 flyer
finding: Four1mN thrusters; specific impulse60-110s; total impulse40Ns;350g wet; average power<2W.
limits: Search-index extraction available; live URL404 and local fetch failed. Values provisional catalogue comparator; obtain current ICD/geometry before selection. Pair lever arm0.15m is this study's assumption.

title: ENPULSION NANO R3 data sheet
finding: 150-350microN;350microN nominal at2500s Isp;5300Ns;45W nominal;30-50W operating;wet mass<1.5kg.
limits: Direct cache download denied403; search extraction reviewed. Not a suitable impulsive1mN RCS substitute without placement and burn-time assessment. No selection implied.

title: NASA SmallSat guidance, navigation and control survey
finding: Storage and slew demands drive wheel choice; wheel imbalance and zero crossings affect jitter; magnetic unloading needs substantial external field.
limits: General guidance, not mission-specific verification.

title: NASA thermal environmental criteria report
finding: Global Earth albedo0.30 and IR237W/m2 with variability; study explicitly warns against treating simple criteria as universal.
limits: Rounded inputs only. Actual orbit thermal-radiation torque needs geography, phase and plate model; do not claim modern climatology or exact peaks.

title: NASA MEM3 software and user guide
finding: Trajectory-dependent flux, direction, speed and density are needed for micrometeoroid risk.
limits: MEM was not run. Study gives conditional individual impulse examples only; no annual collision probability or continuous torque claimed.
